theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Ukraine Reportedly Hits Saratov Oil Refinery in Overnight Strikes
items.lede: A Ukrainian monitoring channel reported fires at Russia's Saratov refinery and near Rostov's Almaz factory overnight, but the reports remain unverified.

sections.text: Monitoring channel Exilenova Plus reported strikes in Russia's Oryol, Saratov, and Rostov regions overnight into 7 November, according to the Kyiv Independent [1]. The outlet said the Saratov Oil Refinery was set ablaze and that a large fire broke out near the Almaz military factory in Rostov [1]. In Oryol, it said the Proton electronic-components factory was targeted; local channels alleged Flamingo missiles, which the Kyiv Independent could not verify [1]. Explosions were also reported in Belgorod, with unclear targets [1]. The Kyiv Independent said the details could not be immediately verified [1]. Separately on Friday, Zelensky said Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russia's oil-refining industry continues in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy sites [2].
Confidence is low: the overnight package rests on a monitoring channel via one outlet that could not verify the details.

items.title: Russian Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv After Zelensky Warning
items.lede: Missile and drone attacks wounded at least three people in Kyiv and its surrounding region overnight after Zelensky warned of mass strikes, Ukrainian officials said.

sections.text: Several waves of Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv overnight on 6–7 November, the Kyiv Independent reported [3]. At least two people were wounded in the city and a third in Kyiv Oblast, authorities said [3]. Ukraine's Air Force reported at least six missiles launched toward Kyiv shortly before 22:00 CET on 6 November [3]. The outlet reported a fresh alert shortly before 23:00 CET on 6 November [3]. It reported further attacks around 00:00, 02:04, and 02:30 CET on 7 November [3]. Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported damage to a five-story residential building, shattered windows elsewhere, a fire at a non-residential building, and damage to a kindergarten in Solomianskyi district [3]. The Kyiv Independent cited Tymur Tkachenko as saying a jet-powered drone attack in Brovary district injured a man with burns and shrapnel wounds [3]. Earlier, President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence pointed to strikes on energy facilities, Dnipro bridges, and civilian infrastructure [4][5]. He urged partners not to delay Patriot interceptor deliveries [4][5]. Attacks were still ongoing in the outlet's 02:45 CET update on 7 November; damage assessments remained incomplete [3].
Confidence is high on the attributed overnight waves and casualty reports from city and oblast officials; figures are Ukrainian claims, not independently verified.

items.title: Brussels Security Talks Draw NATO Confirmation and Kremlin Pushback
items.lede: Critical Threats reiterated that Russian security demands still clash with Kushner's Brussels framework, while Trump said he held Ukraine phone calls Friday and would continue them Saturday.

sections.text: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov said Ukrainian negotiators met in Brussels on Thursday with representatives of France, the United Kingdom, Germany, the United States, and NATO [6][7]. "The main focus of today's meetings in Brussels was security guarantees for Ukraine," he said [6]. CNN reported that NATO Spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed talks among NATO, the United States, Ukraine, and EU and European counterparts ahead of next week's Abu Dhabi trilateral round [8]. CNN also quoted Jared Kushner's Thursday call for a broader European security architecture [8][9]. Critical Threats' 6 November assessment said Kushner's five goals still collide with Moscow's 2021-style NATO rollback demands and rejection of foreign forces in Ukraine [10]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday that Moscow had received no European ideas on security guarantees and that Europeans had not decided who speaks for them [11]. TASS quoted Trump on 7 November saying he held Ukraine-settlement phone calls Friday and planned more Saturday [12]. It also quoted him saying, “We're working well with Russia and Ukraine” [13]. TASS is a Russian state claim-carrier for the Trump quotes; no Western pool transcript was opened [12].
Confidence is high on Umerov, Hart, Peskov, and the Critical Threats framing. Confidence is moderate on Trump's phone-call remarks, which rest on TASS alone.

items.title: Kyiv Faces Prolonged Power and Water Outages After Russian Strikes
items.lede: Overnight attacks struck Kyiv, where Zelensky said Ukraine's energy situation was worst, amid continuing power and water outages.

sections.text: President Volodymyr Zelensky said on 6 November that the situation is worst in Kyiv, where people and businesses face prolonged power and water outages [14]. He blamed Russian strikes on energy infrastructure and a failure to implement city-level heating-season preparations [14]. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said emergency power outages were introduced in Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Chernihiv regions, with Kyiv the hardest case [15]. Overnight 6–7 November ballistic and drone strikes hit residential and infrastructure sites in Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast while the capital was already under prolonged outages [3]. The Moscow Times cited Ukrainian officials reporting Friday outages across seven regions [16]. Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov called the capital region the most difficult, it reported [16]. On 5 November, Kyivvodokanal said power outages had disrupted water across all districts; Mayor Vitali Klitschko later said water pressure was gradually returning [17]. Kyiv's administration said metro service across the Dnipro was suspended around 11:00 CET on 5 November and resumed at 12:05 CET with longer intervals [17].
Confidence is high on Zelensky's and the Energy Ministry's attributed Friday accounts. The overnight attack report does not establish a new outage total.

items.title: Kyiv Says Russia Is Using Its Rassvet Satellite Network Over Ukraine
items.lede: Ukrainian military intelligence told Reuters that Moscow's nascent Starlink-style constellation already supports intermittent military communications aimed at improving strike-drone accuracy.

sections.text: Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate told Reuters that Russia uses Rassvet satellites for military communications over Ukraine. It said the aim is more accurate, jam-resistant strike drones [18]. GUR spokesman Andrii Yusov said Russia launched 32 Rassvet satellites in March and July this year. Coverage remains intermittent; more launches are planned by year-end, he said [18]. GUR said Rassvet may enable two-way data exchange with unmanned aircraft, including mid-flight course changes [18]. Russia's Defense Ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters [18]. Zelensky last week sanctioned ten companies tied to Rassvet, including Bureau 1440 [18].
Confidence is moderate: the claim is a Ukrainian intelligence assertion relayed by Reuters; no Russian confirmation or independent technical corroboration was opened.

items.title: Ukraine Reports One Killed in Russian Attacks and 227 Overnight Drone Launches
items.lede: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 227 long-range attack drones overnight, and regional officials reported one death and more than twenty injuries.

sections.text: Russian attacks across Ukraine killed one person and injured more than twenty over the past day, regional authorities told the Kyiv Independent on 5–6 November [15]. Ukraine's Air Force reported 227 drones launched overnight into 6 November, including 86 jet-powered drones [15]. By about 07:00 CET, it reported 196 intercepted, with impacts at 14 locations and debris at eight others [15]. Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin said three glide bombs and two FPV drones hit Kramatorsk, killing one person [15]. Governors and emergency services also reported injuries in Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Kharkiv, Kherson, Sumy, and Kyiv regions [15]. Mykolaiv Governor Heorhii Reshetilov said Russian forces struck an energy facility there without reported casualties [15]. The Kyiv Independent's headline gives 21 injuries and its body 23; the conflict remains unresolved [15]. This item uses “more than twenty,” not a reconciled total [15].
Confidence is high on the attributed Air Force drone tally and named governors' casualty reports; the figures are Ukrainian official claims, not independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine Says It Struck Two Russian Ammunition Depots in Occupied Zaporizhzhia
items.lede: Ukraine's General Staff said forces hit depots near Melitopol and Khliborobne and also struck a drone command post and a fuel depot in occupied Donetsk.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff reported strikes on 5 November and overnight into 6 November [19][20]. It named ammunition depots near Melitopol and Khliborobne in occupied Zaporizhzhia [19][20]. It also named a UAV control post near Chasiv Yar and a fuel-and-lubricants depot near Luhanske in occupied Donetsk [19][20]. The General Staff said the strikes aimed to reduce Russian firepower and disrupt resupply [20]. The Kyiv Independent and Ukrinform carried the claim [20][21].
Confidence is moderate: the claim rests on Ukraine's General Staff and matching Ukrainian outlets; battle-damage assessment is single-side.

items.title: Komyshuvakha Death Toll From Russian Strike Rises to 53
items.lede: Zaporizhzhia's governor said the toll from Russia's 2 November bombing of a humanitarian-aid site in Komyshuvakha had risen to 53 as searches entered a fifth day.

sections.text: The death toll from Russia's 2 November aerial-bomb attack on Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia Oblast rose to 53, Governor Mykhaylo Semikin said on 6 November, the Kyiv Independent reported [22]. Search and rescue continued for a fifth day, and the final toll was not yet established [22]. Russian forces struck an aid-distribution school and then a shelter holding civilians and rescuers, Ukrainian officials said [22]. Zelensky said one bomb was a FAB-3000 and nine further bombs hit the shelter [22]. Interfax-Ukraine also carried the 53 figure [23].
Confidence is high on the attributed governor toll as carried by two Ukrainian outlets; the final count remains open while searches continue.

items.title: Zelensky Says Spain Will Provide 437 Million Euros in Military Aid
items.lede: On Friday Zelensky again cited Spain's new defense package and said Germany would provide winter energy-resilience support after his Madrid visit.

sections.text: After bilateral talks in Madrid on 5 November, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Spain would deliver a new military aid package worth 437 million euros, about $490 million [24]. "Throughout this war, Spain has consistently provided us with assistance and support," he said [24]. The Kyiv Independent reported the funds would help bolster Ukrainian air defenses [24]. Zelensky also met King Felipe VI and said Ukraine was represented at the Ibero-American Summit for the first time, Kyiv Post reported [25]. On 6 November Zelensky posted that the Spanish package would help Ukrainian forces and that Germany would provide a winter support package for resilience, especially energy [26]. He said partners were also working to accelerate Patriot missiles, IRIS-T systems, and F-16 assistance [26]. The Spanish government confirms the Madrid meeting, not the 437-million-euro military figure [27].

Confidence is high that Zelensky announced the Spanish package and the German winter claim on the record; delivery of both remains prospective. Berlin confirmation of the winter package was not opened this run.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Bulgaria Says It Destroyed Drone Identified as Russian Gerber-2
items.lede: A Navy team found no explosives in an unmarked craft washed ashore near Cape Shabla, the Defense Ministry said.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Defense Ministry said a Varna Naval Base team destroyed a drone found near Shabla on 6 November [1][2]. BTA and the Sofia Globe reported the northern Black Sea coast operation [1][2]. The Interior Ministry reported the find at 09:00 CET on the beach north of the Cape Shabla lighthouse [1]. Specialists said the aerial drone probably fell into the sea and washed ashore; the hull had no inscriptions and was classified as a Russian Gerber-2 [1][2]. It carried no explosive and was destroyed on site under safety procedures [1]. The Sofia Globe said the incident was among more than 100 drone or drone-part finds in Bulgarian waters or on beaches since the start of 2026 [2].

Confidence is high on the attributed Bulgarian Defense Ministry account as carried by BTA and the Sofia Globe. The Russian identification rests on the ministry's assessment, not an independent inspection.

items.title: Europe Bomb Hoaxes Hit More Flights and Irish Newsrooms
items.lede: Friday's threats reached newsrooms as Reuters reported an unverified email signature, while ISW estimated more than 50 aviation threats that week.

sections.text: Further Friday bomb threats disrupted at least another 18 flights across several European countries, the Guardian reported [3]. The Guardian reported safe landings and no explosives on flights it covered [3]. The Guardian's reopened 5 November article distinguishes at least 25 Thursday threats from 34 affected flights that week [4]. Earlier 25/34/33 conflicts belong to previous versions, not a current reconciled total [4]. Al Jazeera reported at least 17 flights disrupted by 13:00 CET on 6 November [5]. Threats targeted RTÉ, the Irish Independent, Newstalk, and Virgin Media [6][7]. BBC reported evacuations at the first three; Virgin Media said it stayed on air without evacuating [6]. Ireland's Department of the Taoiseach called the threats "very serious" and said a coordinated disruption campaign seemed likely [8]. Reuters' Friday wrap said newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed threats from a purported "Mikhail Andropov," headlined "Message to the West," claiming responsibility for the aviation wave [9]. Reuters could not establish the sender's identity [9]. Critical Threats estimated more than 50 aviation bomb threats during the week of 2 November [10]. It said European states had not attributed the campaign to a specific actor [10].

Confidence is high on the reported disruptions and scoped Irish evacuations, but moderate on flight totals with different cutoffs and denominators. Sender identity and state attribution remain unestablished.

items.title: Moldova's Security Council Sets Cyber Fixes After Attack Hit 450,000 People
items.lede: President Maia Sandu said a cyberattack on government systems accessed data of more than 450,000 citizens and ordered a prime-minister-led working group to propose fixes within a month.

sections.text: Moldova's National Security Council met on 6 November after an October cyberattack on government information systems, Moldpres reported [11]. President Maia Sandu said attackers exploited authentication and access-control weaknesses in Electronic Governance Agency infrastructure [11]. They accessed registers of at least ten institutions and over 450,000 citizens’ data, she said [11]. Automated requests from more than 638 IP addresses began on the evening of 19 October [11]. About one million requests and over 260,000 extracted kinship records followed on 20 October; blocking finished by 24 October [11]. Sandu said a working group led by Prime Minister Vasile Tofan has one month to propose systemic cybersecurity solutions, with a follow-up NSC review in three months [11][12][13]. Sandu described frequent cyberattacks as part of Russia’s hybrid-warfare arsenal against Europe [11]. She said the pattern could point to a state actor but named no country, citing no evidence on who was behind it [13]. A criminal case has been opened [11].
Confidence is high on the attributed Sandu figures and NSC measures from Moldpres and IPN. State attribution for the October intrusion was not established in the opened accounts.

items.title: Dutch Police Estimate 150–200 Arrests at Amsterdam Microsoft Datacenter Protest
items.lede: Activists breached a Westpoort construction site, climbed a crane, and clashed with riot police, NOS and the Guardian reported.

sections.text: Dutch police estimated that 150–200 people were arrested for suspected trespassing at Microsoft's Westpoort construction site, NOS reported [1]. Fossielvrij rallied at a designated spot nearby [1]. Another group breached fences; protesters later entered the construction site, climbed a crane, and reached a roof, NOS said [1]. Police told NOS they tried to stop the occupation, used force, and later cleared the site; they reported damage and alleged theft of materials [1]. The Guardian reported that Geef Tegengas activists entered the site amid Europe-wide datacenter protests [2]. Protesters said police used force and tear gas [2]. Banners protested Microsoft's work for the Israeli military and U.S. immigration enforcement, the Guardian reported [2]. Police said the suspects were taken to a detention facility, with a continued-custody decision expected Friday evening [1].
Confidence is high on the police's attributed arrest estimate and the reported breach, not an independently counted total. Activist motives and military-contract claims remain allegations.

items.title: EU Prosecutors Probe Spain's Rail Funds After the Urda Crash
items.lede: Guardia Civil specialists sought documents at Adif, the rail-safety agency, and Spain's Court of Auditors on Friday.

sections.text: The European Public Prosecutor's Office opened a suspected EU-funds fraud investigation concerning Spain's Madrid–Seville high-speed line, BBC, RTVE, and El País reported [3][4][5]. It concerns funds for renewing safety, signaling, and communications systems [3][4][5]. EPPO said it was acting after the 28 October Urda crash that killed 69 people [3]. Spain's Guardia Civil UCO unit collected documents Friday at Adif, the State Railway Safety Agency, and the Court of Auditors [4][5]. It is EPPO's second EU-funds inquiry on the line this year after the January Adamuz crash that killed 46 [3][4]. BBC noted the LZB train-positioning system had failed before the Urda collision [3]. EPPO said it would release no further details for now [3]. Guilt and any fund misuse remain unproven.
Confidence is high on EPPO's attributed opening of the inquiry and the Friday document requests as reported by BBC, RTVE, and El País. The inquiry does not establish fraud or guilt.

items.title: Italy's Former ILVA Steelworks Shuts Down Hot-Production Facilities
items.lede: Acciaieria d'Italia's director general reported a hot-production shutdown after the Court of Cassation ruling, as temporary-layoff talks were adjourned to 10 November.

sections.text: Taranto's former ILVA steelworks shut all hot-production facilities Friday, director general Maurizio Saitta told unions [6][7][8]. ANSA, RAI News, and Sky TG24 reported remarks by the director general of Acciaieria d'Italia, which is under state-appointed administration [6][7][8]. "As of this morning, nothing is running any more. All the facilities in the hot section have been shut down," he said at a Labor Ministry meeting on temporary layoffs [6][7]. Shutdown procedures began after the Court of Cassation rejected appeals against a Milan court order last week [6]. The order required hot-production facilities to stop within three months unless asbestos was removed and particulate emissions brought within safe limits [6]. Acciaierie d'Italia sought temporary layoff coverage for up to 8,622 workers through 28 February 2027 [7][8]. Friday's ministry talks ended without agreement and were adjourned to Tuesday, 10 November [7][8].
Confidence is high on the shutdown and Saitta's attributed remarks as carried by ANSA and Italian public and commercial broadcasters. Future ownership and decarbonization funding remain contested.

items.title: France Announces 70,000 Officers for Saturday Protests
items.lede: Nuñez announced Saturday security plans as youth groups and Yellow Vests planned protests, with union wage talks scheduled for Monday.

sections.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced 70,000 police and gendarmes across France for Saturday, 7 November, matching Thursday's deployment, RTBF reported [9][10][11]. This renews the announced plan used since 24 October; it is not an observed Saturday headcount [9]. Nuñez said prefects had banned some city-center demonstrations and that armored vehicles, water cannons, drones, and helicopters would be deployed [9]. Nuñez gave a newer tally of 642 arrests for Thursday's nationwide protests [9]. The earlier 448 arrests and 53 injured officers were provisional as of 18:00 CET on 5 November [10]. Authorities' final Thursday turnout was 575,000 across 193 marches; CGT claimed about 1.6 million [10][11]. France 24 English still reports 60,000 in Paris; its French article and RTBF report 65,000 [9][10][11]. Actu.fr listed 86 planned Saturday action sites on Yellow Vest organizers' maps, including 70 marches [12]. Farandou told TF1 Friday it was important to try raising the monthly net minimum wage above 1,500 euros, Les Echos reported [13]. It is currently about 1,478 euros; he said nothing was settled [13]. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu still plans a social conference with unions and employers on Monday, 9 November [10][14].

Confidence is high on Nuñez's announced Saturday deployment and attributed arrest figures via RTBF, and on Farandou's TF1 remarks. Saturday turnout is prospective. Organizer maps are plans, not authorizations. Smic policy remains undecided.

items.title: Belgium's King Refuses De Wever's Resignation, Orders Budget Talks
items.lede: De Wever plans to resume budget talks Monday, with each deputy prime minister allowed one extra person, before reporting to the palace on 16 November.

sections.text: Belgium's Royal Palace said King Philippe refused Bart De Wever's resignation on 6 November and ordered immediate budget talks [15][16][17]. De Wever is to report back on Monday 16 November [15][16]. After meeting the five governing-party leaders, the palace said each pledged to finish talks as soon as possible and to make concessions for a multi-year budget path [15][16]. VRT reported that budget talks would resume Monday, with each deputy prime minister allowed one extra person, potentially a party chair [18]. De Wever offered his resignation Monday after the Arizona coalition failed to agree a 2027 budget [16]. He had told parliament Belgium faces another year of temporary monthly budgets [16].
Confidence is high on the palace refusal and 16 November return as carried by multiple major outlets and Belgium's public broadcaster. The +1 format is process reporting, not proof of a deal.

items.title: Spain's Police Detain 14 in Raid on Far-Right Núcleo Nacional
items.lede: Investigators link the case to February unrest in Gijón that injured students, El País and RTVE reported.

sections.text: Spain's National Police detained 14 members of the far-right group Núcleo Nacional on Friday and searched its Madrid headquarters, El País and RTVE reported [19][20]. Judicial sources cited by El País said the probe began after February clashes near a Jesuit school in Gijón that injured several students [19]. Suspects are under investigation for hate crimes, unlawful association, and weapons possession [19][20]. RTVE reported that seven possible leaders would be questioned in Asturias, provisionally Sunday, 8 November, or Monday, 9 November [20]. Operations ran in Madrid, Asturias, Guadalajara, Valladolid, Pontevedra, Burgos, and Alicante [19][20]. RTVE said police confirmed the action on social media and that the investigation remains open [20].
Confidence is high on the detention tally and alleged offenses as attributed to police and Asturias judicial sources in El País and RTVE. Guilt is unproven.

items.title: EU Charges TikTok Over Algorithm Risks to Users' Mental Health
items.lede: A preliminary Digital Services Act finding says the app's feed can push young users into harmful content loops.

sections.text: The European Commission on Friday issued a preliminary Digital Services Act finding that TikTok failed to protect users' mental health, the Guardian reported [21]. Officials said the algorithm can be harmful and lead young and vulnerable users "down rabbit holes they cannot easily escape from," Commission tech lead Henna Virkkunen said [21]. The probe focused on legal videos whose cumulative effect on themes such as body image or isolation may worsen anxiety or eating disorders [21]. TikTok, with about 189 million EU users, called the statements inaccurate and said users have controls [21]. A confirmed breach could bring a fine of up to 6% of global turnover [21]. The Commission had already preliminarily faulted TikTok's "addictive design," including infinite scroll [21].
Confidence is high on the preliminary finding as reported by the Guardian from Commission statements. No Commission press-corner HTML was opened this run.

items.title: EU and UK Near a Deal to Link Their Carbon Markets
items.lede: A draft seen by Euronews points to an announcement at the 20 November Brussels summit, with mutual ETS recognition.

sections.text: The European Union and the United Kingdom are preparing to link their emissions trading systems, according to a draft document seen by Euronews [22]. The draft anticipates an announcement at the 20 November EU–UK summit [22]. Mutual allowance recognition would pave the way for exemptions from each other’s carbon border charges [22]. Officials argue energy-intensive industries could avoid double carbon costs after the EU border mechanism began in January 2026 and a UK system is due in January 2027 [22]. British MP Henry Tufnell (named David by Euronews) told Euronews linkage could push UK carbon prices toward higher EU levels [22]. The draft can still change before publication [22].
Confidence is moderate: the story rests on a draft document seen by one major outlet, not a published joint communiqué.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Lithuania's Nausėda Joins NB8 Call With Zelensky
items.lede: The Lithuanian president said Europe must fully join Ukraine peace talks and agree a common mandate before Abu Dhabi diplomacy.

sections.text: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda joined a Friday conference call with Nordic-Baltic Eight leaders and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky, LRT reported, citing ELTA and the presidency [1]. They discussed diplomatic initiatives to end the war in Ukraine, keeping pressure on Russia, and next international steps [1]. Nausėda said Europe must fully participate in talks on peace in Ukraine and its future security architecture [1]. Europe first needs a common position and clear negotiating mandate, he said [1]. With a new Abu Dhabi diplomatic round approaching, he said transatlantic unity must hold so Russia cannot use talks to ease international pressure [1]. He urged more support for Ukraine and priority agreement on a 22nd EU sanctions package against Russia [1]. "Current support for Ukraine is not enough," he said, calling for long-term military and financial aid [1]. The presidency said Lithuania's cumulative military aid to Ukraine is 1.2 billion euros, including 209 million euros this year [1].
Confidence is high on the attributed Nausėda remarks as carried by LRT via ELTA and the presidency. No second English wire was opened.

items.title: Chinese Diplomats Plan Lithuania Visit to Discuss Restoring Representation
items.lede: Lawmaker Ignas Vėgėlė gave 11–12 November as the proposed dates for meetings with ministry officials and parliamentary representatives.

sections.text: Chinese diplomats are due in Lithuania next week to discuss restoring ambassador-level representation with Beijing, lawmaker Ignas Vėgėlė told BNS on Friday, LRT reported [2]. He said the visit is set for 11–12 November and that China now sees Lithuanian interest in repairing ties [2]. The visitors are to meet Foreign Ministry officials and a Seimas group seeking to normalize China ties to the EU-member standard, he said [2]. Seimas Foreign Affairs Committee chair Remigijus Motuzas told LRT Radio the meetings are working-level diplomatic consultations without state or political weight [2]. Lithuania's Foreign Ministry told BNS it had no new information on the China talks [2]. China downgraded diplomatic representation after Vilnius allowed a Taiwanese Representative Office in 2021 [2]. Lithuania later stopped new Chinese accreditations, leaving no Chinese diplomats in the country since May 2025 [2]. Visit timing rests on Vėgėlė via BNS/LRT; the MFA declined comment [2].
Confidence is moderate: the schedule rests on an interested-party lawmaker via BNS/LRT, and Lithuania's Foreign Ministry declined to confirm.

items.title: Lithuania Says Kaliningrad Border Is Calmer Than Poland's
items.lede: Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said troops helping border guards since 8 October will likely stay beyond mid-November if intelligence warrants.

sections.text: Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas told Žinių radijas Friday that the Kaliningrad border was calmer than Poland’s side [3]. Kaunas said Polish authorities had thwarted a potential provocation [3]. Lithuanian troops have backed the State Border Guard Service on that border since 8 October [3]. Kaunas extended the help to mid-November and said another extension is likely if intelligence still warrants it [3]. "Currently, the situation on the border with Kaliningrad is certainly calmer than it was in Poland, let's say, and we are reacting accordingly," he said [3]. President Gitanas Nausėda declined detailed public comment, saying revealing intelligence would help hostile services [3].
Confidence is high: Kaunas spoke on the record to Lithuanian media as carried by LRT/BNS.

items.title: Lithuania Auditor Warns Deficit Could Near 6% of GDP
items.lede: The National Audit Office said the 2027–2029 draft budget breaches national and EU fiscal rules even with a defense carve-out.

sections.text: Lithuania's National Audit Office said Friday the draft budget for 2027–2029 was prepared outside national and EU fiscal rules [4]. It warned the general government deficit could approach 6% of GDP by 2029, faster than the government projects, and that public debt could near the 60% Maastricht line [4]. Planned net spending growth in 2026–2029 exceeds limits even with a temporary defense exemption, and the draft shows deficits above 3% of GDP each year, it said [4]. The watchdog urged the government to revise the draft to meet fiscal rules or explain the deviations [4].
Confidence is high: the warning comes from Lithuania's National Audit Office via LRT/BNS.

items.title: Latvia's Kulbergs Cabinet Says It Hit Most Action-Plan Goals
items.lede: The State Chancellery counted 52 of 61 priority tasks done by 15 October, and Kulbergs said a change of government should not halt that work.

sections.text: Latvia's Cabinet on 6 November reviewed a State Chancellery report on the Kulbergs government's action plan [5]. By 15 October it said 52 of 61 priority ministerial tasks (85%) and 132 of 185 plan measures (71%) were completed [5]. Fifty measures remain "in the process of implementation" [5]. Three had not started: two education measures await 2027 budget funding, and a study did not back aid for energy-intensive firms [5]. Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List) said the figures cover security, bureaucracy cuts, the business climate, and welfare, and that a government change should not stop work already started [5]. LSM noted "implementation" often means work begun, not finished [5].
Confidence is high on the Chancellery counts as reported by LSM; the meaning of "completed" is the government's own scoring.

items.title: Latvia Hosts Electronic Warfare Coalition Session for Ukraine
items.lede: Parliamentary Secretary Karina Ploka said Latvia offers the Sēlija range for testing electronic-warfare gear and training for Ukraine.

sections.text: Latvia's Defense Ministry said a plenary of the Electronic Warfare Coalition met in Latvia this week to discuss current challenges and support for Ukraine [6]. Karina Ploka, parliamentary secretary at the ministry, said Allied help on electronic warfare protects Ukrainian forces, critical infrastructure, cities, and civilians [6]. She said Latvia contributes by offering the Sēlija military training ground for operational testing of electronic-warfare equipment and technologies, and for training that also involves local industry [6]. Coalition members visited Sēlija during the session [6]. The coalition was formed in April 2025 under the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, has 15 members including Latvia, and is led by Germany with Sweden and Ukraine [6].
Confidence is high: the account rests on Latvia's Defense Ministry as carried by LSM.

items.title: New US Cavalry Troop Rotation Arrives in Estonia
items.lede: The US Embassy said Apache Troop, 5th Squadron, 4th Cavalry Regiment is on a planned nine-month Baltic rotation.

sections.text: A new U.S. Army rotation is in Estonia after a summer gap, ERR reported [7]. Embassy spokesperson Kelli Long confirmed Apache Troop, 5th Squadron, 4th Cavalry Regiment for a standard nine-month rotation [7]. She said an uncasing ceremony later this month in Lithuania will formally mark the unit's presence across the Baltics [7]. Defence Minister Martin Herem said the advance team and equipment have been in Estonia for more than a week [7]. The prior U.S. unit left in summer amid a Pentagon review of forces in Europe, then-minister Hanno Pevkur had said [7].
Confidence is high: the unit designation and rotation terms come from the U.S. Embassy and Estonia's defence minister via ERR.

items.title: Lithuania Hosts More Than 6,000 Troops in German-Led Drills
items.lede: Freedom Shield 26-II and Grand Eagle 26 run through 3 December at two Lithuanian training areas, the armed forces said.

sections.text: Lithuania’s Armed Forces said two German-led exercises involving more than 6,000 troops were scheduled to begin on 6 November and continue until 3 December [8]. Freedom Shield 26-II is at Rūdninkai. Grand Eagle 26 is at the General Silvestras Žukauskas training area [8]. Germany's 45th Armoured Brigade Lietuva and 37th Mechanised Infantry Brigade Freistaat Sachsen, both under the 10th Armoured Division, lead the drills [8]. Troops from Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, the Czech Republic, Croatia, Belgium, and Luxembourg in NATO's Multinational Combat Brigade in Lithuania join a Lithuanian unit [8]. The military warned of heavy convoy traffic from Kalvarija on 6–7 November and from Klaipėda on 10–12 November, with return moves 28 November–3 December [8].
Confidence is high: the exercise details come from Lithuania's Armed Forces via LRT/BNS.

items.title: Estonia Clears Turkish Firm for Ammunition Plant Permit
items.lede: ARCA Baltics Operations aims to start large-caliber production in 2028 at Põhja-Kiviõli, with a planned €300 million investment.

sections.text: Turkish defense company ARCA has an Estonian operating permit for a planned ammunition factory at Põhja-Kiviõli, ERR reported [9]. ARCA Baltics Operations received the permit on 20 October and is to begin production in 2028 [9]. The firm plans to invest €300 million and create up to 1,000 jobs making large-caliber rounds, including 155-millimeter artillery shells, for use by Estonia's Defense Forces [9]. The state is to provide a 141-hectare site in the defense industry park and invest up to €10 million in roads, fencing, and utilities [9]. A property-rights deal is targeted before a notary by year-end, a Defence Ministry spokesperson said [9]. ERR noted prior corruption suspicions around ARCA's founder; the ministry said the companies meet bidding rules requiring no current criminal convictions for key persons [9].
Confidence is high on the permit and investment figures as reported by ERR from ministry and company statements. Prior suspicions are noted separately from current convictions.

items.title: Lithuania Teachers Union Sets 16 November Strike Over Pay
items.lede: The union wants a 10% rise in salary coefficients and rejects the ministry's proposed 7.56% increase for next year.

sections.text: Lithuania's Education Workers' Trade Union (LŠDPS) said Friday it will start a nationwide teachers' strike on 16 November unless an agreement on pay rises is reached [10]. Chairman Andrius Navickas said the Education, Science and Sports Ministry's plan for a 7.56% rise next year, about 92 to 152 euros a month after tax, is not enough [10]. The union demands a 10% increase in teachers' salary coefficients [10]. "Teachers are not inclined to strike for the sake of striking," Navickas said, arguing decisions were already made without real dialogue [10].
Confidence is high: the strike plan and figures come from the union chairman via LRT/BNS.

items.title: Serbian Prosecutors Seek Detention in Vojvodina Housing Case
items.lede: The request concerns Predrag Vuletić and Dragan Milisavljević over alleged subsidy losses of 130.9 million dinars, N1 reported.

sections.text: Novi Sad's Higher Public Prosecutor's Office anti-corruption unit requested detention Friday evening, N1 reported [1]. The request concerns Vojvodina social-policy secretary Predrag Vuletić and commission chair Dragan Milisavljević [1]. Prosecutors say unlawful housing-subsidy awards cost the Vojvodina budget 130.9 million dinars [1]. They cite flight risk and witness-influence risk for both men, and repeat-offense risk for Vuletić [1]. Both face allegations of continuing abuse of office [1]. They were brought in and questioned within the legal deadline after up to 48 hours' prior holding [1]. N1 reports prosecutors' allegations, not a conviction [1].
Confidence is high on the attributed prosecutor detention request as reported by N1. The source describes a detention request, not a court order; guilt is unproven.

items.title: EU Opens Roam-Like-at-Home Talks With Balkans
items.lede: Bilateral talks cover Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, the Commission said.

sections.text: The European Commission said it opened bilateral negotiations to bring Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia into the EU's Roam Like at Home regime [2]. Travelers between the EU and Western Balkans would make calls, send texts, and use mobile data without roaming surcharges [2]. This requires finalized agreements and alignment with EU roaming rules [2]. The Commission would then ask the Council to extend the roaming area [2]. The Council authorized the talks in June 2026; agreements would rest on existing Stabilisation and Association Agreements [2]. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen previewed the step during an October Western Balkans trip [2]. N1 reported that Serbia's caretaker government accepted a negotiating-team report on joining the EU roaming regime the previous Friday [3].
Confidence is high on the Commission's attributed opening of talks naming all six Western Balkan partners. Final agreements and Council extension remain prospective.

items.title: Serbia's Student List Seeks Probe of Alleged Vučić Crime Links
items.lede: The election winners asked Serbia's top prosecutor and the organized-crime prosecutor to open cases on Radar magazine allegations.

sections.text: Serbia's winning Student List – Students Win asked prosecutors Friday evening to investigate alleged Vučić links to organized crime, N1 reported [4]. It addressed Supreme Public Prosecutor Zagorka Dolovac and organized-crime prosecutor Mladen Nenadić over Radar weekly's allegations about the former president [4]. They say the 22 October Radar piece raised matters of public interest and that prosecutors have not yet opened a case [4]. The students link Vučić in that account to groups associated with Darko Šarić and Veljko Belivuk — allegations, not proven facts [4]. They asked Dolovac to assign a prosecutor for a pre-investigation and asked Nenadić to open a file and gather documents [4]. The students said the Interior Ministry holds Sky app chats and cited communications involving Europol and Eurojust [4]. They said French authorities would stop accepting Sky-data assistance requests through Eurojust or diplomatic channels from 1 December 2026 [4]. Earlier requests would still be fulfilled, they said [4]. The statement is Student List advocacy; Radar's allegations remain unproven [4].
Confidence is high on the attributed Student List demand as reported by N1. The underlying Radar allegations and Sky-chat claims remain unproven.

items.title: EU-Western Balkan Ministers Press Corruption Results in Budva
items.lede: N1 reported calls for prosecutions, final judgments, and asset confiscation in high-level corruption cases at the Budva forum.

sections.text: N1 reported EU calls for concrete corruption-investigation, prosecution, and final-conviction results at the Budva forum in Montenegro on 5–6 November [5]. High-level cases and asset confiscation were included [5]. Talks also covered links between corruption and organized crime, whistleblower laws, and deeper work with Eurojust and the European Public Prosecutor's Office [5]. The Council joint release framed online child sexual abuse, cybercrime, migrant smuggling, and visa alignment as core themes, with Ireland's Jim O'Callaghan and Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath co-chairing [6].
Confidence is high on the agenda and chairs from the Council release and on the corruption-results call as reported by N1 from the forum.

items.title: Serbia's Election Commission Assigns Seats and Closes Its Role
items.lede: RIK gave the Student List 140 seats and Vučić's list 103, and said the constitutive Assembly session comes next.

sections.text: Serbia's Republic Election Commission proclaimed final results of the 25 October snap parliamentary election on the evening of 5 November, N1 reported [7]. RIK published the certification [8]. On 6 November RIK assigned mandates and then unanimously adopted its report on the election, N1 reported [9][10]. Student List – Students Win receives 140 seats. United Serbia – Aleksandar Vučić receives 103 [9]. Minority lists: Alliance of Vojvodina Hungarians (2), Albanian Coalition (2), Rasim Ljajić – Human (1), Usame Zukorlić – Movement for Unification (1), and SDA – Guardians of Sandžak (1) [9]. RIK President Vladimir Dimitrijević said adopting the report ends the commission's role for this election and that the constitutive session of the new Assembly follows [10]. Repeat voting on 1 November covered 53 stations [10].
Confidence is high on RIK's published certification, mandate assignment, and final report as carried by N1. These are certified results, not an independent ballot audit.

items.title: Euronews Profiles Serbia Student List Envoy Srdanović
items.lede: Cardiologist Ilija Srdanović has taken calls from Macron, Costa, Plenković, and others since the Student List's election win.

sections.text: Euronews on Friday profiled Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist who became European leaders' main contact after the Student List won 140 of 250 seats on 25 October [11]. French President Emmanuel Macron wrote on X that he spoke with Srdanović and restated France's support for Serbia's European path [11]. Euronews said European Council President António Costa, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, Hungary's Péter Magyar, North Macedonia's Hristijan Mickoski, and Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos also reached the list largely through him [11]. The piece stresses it is still unclear whether he will lead a future government [11]. Separately, Student List figure Marko Đenadić told Demostat the list has several prime-minister candidates but will not name them yet, and that outgoing speaker Ana Brnabić has 30 days after final results to call the constitutive Assembly session [12].
Confidence is high on the Euronews profile and attributed Macron outreach; whether Srdanović will lead a government remains unsettled.

items.title: Serbia Court Detains Anti-Terror Unit Chief Over Protest Abuse
items.lede: A Belgrade court ordered up to 30 days' custody for Igor Zmiric and eight other current or former Interior Ministry staff.

sections.text: Balkan Insight reported a Belgrade court ordered up to 30 days’ detention for nine current or former Interior Ministry employees Friday [13]. They include Special Anti-Terrorist Unit commander Igor Zmiric [13]. Prosecutors accuse them of jointly committing abuse and torture against students and others in the government-building garage between about 22:30 on 14 August 2025 and 01:00 on 15 August [13]. The court cited witness-influence risk, offense seriousness, and public concern [13]. Among the nine is retired officer Milan Vukovic, now acting head of the detention facility holding former JZO chief Marko Kricak, who faces a separate murder-related case [13]. N1, citing Danas, reported a Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office commission took over prominent files, including the government-garage abuse case [14]. A first public report is expected on 9 November [14].
Confidence is high on the remand order as reported by BIRN and on the commission step as reported by N1. Allegations remain unproven.

items.title: Kosovo Assembly Seats Serb List Deputies on Committees
items.lede: Srpske Novine said the package vote ended a mid-October blockade after Self-Determination lawmakers participated.

sections.text: Srpske Novine reported Serb List deputies’ committee appointments, citing Koha and KoSSev [15]. Its account gives conflicting 5–6 November vote dates; the exact date remains unresolved [15]. The proposal passed 63–0 with one abstention after governing Self-Determination joined the vote, Srpske Novine reported [15]. Earlier attempts had treated Serb candidates separately and failed for lack of participation [15]. This time Serb List names were bundled with other groups' committee changes [15]. The Serb List holds nine of ten Serb-reserved seats and had held no committee posts [15]. The Kosovo Democratic Institute had warned that keeping Serbs off committees limited constitutionally guaranteed representation [15].
Confidence is moderate: the English wrap rests on Srpske Novine citing Koha and KoSSev; those primary pages were not independently fetched this run.

items.title: EPPO Says Novi Sad EU-Funds Probe Is Still Open
items.lede: The European Public Prosecutor's Office told N1 it would withhold further details to protect its ongoing investigation.

sections.text: The European Public Prosecutor's Office confirmed to N1 that its investigation into possible misuse of EU funds tied to Novi Sad railway station remains open [16]. "The investigation is still ongoing and at this moment we cannot share more information, so as not to jeopardize proceedings under way and their outcome," EPPO told N1 [16]. The office first confirmed the probe in March 2025, saying it can act when EU financial interests are harmed even if the acts occurred in a non-member country [16]. Andrés Ritter became European chief prosecutor on 1 November, succeeding Laura Kövesi [16]. The station canopy collapse killed 16 people on 1 November 2024 and helped trigger Serbia’s protest movement, Euronews reported [11].
Confidence is high on EPPO's on-record confirmation to N1 that the probe remains open.

items.title: China's Vice President Han Zheng Meets Georgia's Prime Minister in Tbilisi
items.lede: Irakli Kobakhidze hosted talks and an official dinner during Han Zheng's visit, scheduled to last through 8 November.

sections.text: Chinese Vice President Han Zheng met Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze in Tbilisi on 6 November, Interpressnews and Georgian Public Broadcaster 1TV reported [1][2]. Kobakhidze thanked China for supporting Georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity and restated Georgia's One China position [1][2]. He said China is Georgia's largest investor this year and pressed deeper Belt and Road, trade, and sector ties [1][2]. Han Zheng said strategic relations are growing stronger and that China supports Georgia's sovereignty, security, and development [3]. Kobakhidze later hosted Han Zheng and the Chinese delegation at an official dinner [4]. Han Zheng met Georgian Dream President Mikheil Kavelashvili earlier on 6 November during his visit, scheduled through 8 November [5][6]. He is expected in Turkey for COP31 after Georgia [5]. 1TV attributes its dinner report to the Georgian prime minister's press service [4].
Confidence is high: the Kobakhidze meeting and dinner rest on Georgian government readouts carried by IPN and 1TV; the earlier Kavelashvili meeting rests on Civil.ge.

items.title: Azerbaijan and Ukraine Adopt a 2026–2027 Economic Action Plan in Uzhhorod
items.lede: Energy ministers adopted a 14-sector plan and noted about $52 million in Azerbaijani aid since Russia's full-scale invasion.

sections.text: Azerbaijan and Ukraine held their 14th Joint Intergovernmental Commission on Economic Cooperation in Uzhhorod on 6 November, APA and Euronews reported [7][8]. It was the first session on Ukrainian soil since Russia’s full-scale invasion [8]. Azerbaijani Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov and Ukrainian First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal co-chaired the talks [7][8]. They signed a protocol and adopted a 2026–2027 plan covering 14 areas, including energy, trade, investment, transport, and technology [7][8]. Officials said bilateral trade rose 10.5% in the first eight months of 2026, with Azerbaijani exports to Ukraine up 17%, and mutual investments at $513.5 million [7][8]. Shmyhal thanked Baku for grid-repair gear, including a recent package valued at about $1.47 million with transformers, cable, and generators [8]. Azerbaijan's humanitarian, rehabilitation, and reconstruction aid to Ukraine was put at about $52 million since the war began [7][8]. APA is an Azerbaijani news agency [7].
Confidence is high: both capitals' ministers are on the record; APA and Euronews carry the same core acts.

items.title: Pashinyan Says Armenia and Turkey Will Establish Diplomatic Ties Soon
items.lede: Speaking at the Global Armenian Summit, he tied recognition of each other's borders and sovereignty to the expected step.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on 6 November that Armenia and Turkey will establish diplomatic relations soon, Armenpress and Anadolu Agency reported [9][10]. He spoke at the Global Armenian Summit 2026 in reply to a participant's question [9]. Pashinyan said he was confident Armenia and Turkey would soon establish diplomatic ties while recognizing each other’s territorial integrity, sovereignty, and borders, Armenpress reported [9]. The land border has been closed since 1993; special envoys have led a normalization track since late 2021 [10]. Anadolu Agency noted Erdoğan invited Pashinyan to COP31 in Turkey during a September UN meeting [10]. Armenpress is the Armenian state agency [9].
Confidence is high: the remark is on the record and mirrored by Armenpress and Turkey's state agency AA.

items.title: Armenia's Constitutional Court Elects Former Ruling-Party Lawmaker as President
items.lede: Vladimir Vardanyan won a second-round vote; rights groups say the court's independence is now harder to trust.

sections.text: Armenia's Constitutional Court elected Vladimir Vardanyan as its president on Friday, OC Media reported [11]. Vardanyan is a former Civil Contract member of parliament who joined the court as a judge earlier in 2026; all sitting judges were appointed during Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's tenure [11]. He and Vice President Edgar Shatiryan were the only candidates; a 14 October ballot failed to produce a winner [11]. After Friday's result, Shatiryan resigned as vice president but said he would stay as a judge [11]. Helsinki Citizens' Assembly Vanadzor's Artur Sakunts questioned how anyone can approach the court with confidence; Journalists' Club Asparez chair Levon Barseghyan called the election "yet another disgrace" [11]. Fourteen civil-society groups had opposed Vardanyan's March judicial appointment over his prior party role [11].
Confidence is high on the election result as reported by OC Media; the independence critique is attributed opinion.

items.title: ALDE Backs Georgia's Droa After Russia Labels the Party Undesirable
items.lede: The European liberal alliance backed the jailed opposition leader's party and recalled that Russia had designated ALDE itself as undesirable last year.

sections.text: The Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe expressed solidarity with Georgia's Droa party after Russia's 5 November "undesirable" designation, Georgia Today reported on 6 November [12]. ALDE said its member party was targeted for opposing occupation, defending Georgia's sovereignty, and backing a European future [12]. "We stand firmly with Droa and everyone fighting for a free, democratic and European Georgia," the statement said [12]. ALDE noted that it and its youth wing LYMEC received the same Russian designation last year [12]. Droa leader Elene Khoshtaria is imprisoned in Georgia [12].
Confidence is moderate: the ALDE quote is on the record but carried so far by one Tbilisi English outlet.

items.title: Georgia's Ivanishvili Meets Israel's Ambassador at the Georgian Dream Office
items.lede: The ruling-party founder discussed bilateral ties; the embassy restated Israel's support for Georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

sections.text: Georgian Dream founder and honorary chairman Bidzina Ivanishvili met Israel's Ambassador Walid Abu Haya at the party's central office on 6 November, Civil Georgia reported [13]. The party said they discussed "special friendship," positive cooperation, and the role of diplomacy in regional stability [13]. The Israeli Embassy said Abu Haya appreciated the meeting, discussed cooperation prospects, and "reiterated Israel's support for Georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity" [13]. Levan Karumidze of the National Gastronomy Agency also attended [13]. Ivanishvili holds no formal government office; he is labeled here as party founder and honorary chairman [13].
Confidence is moderate: the readout is party and embassy statements in one independent outlet; no third-party wire yet.

items.title: Pistorius Says Germany May Meet Staffing Goals Without Conscription
items.lede: The defense minister made his forecast conditional on the current recruitment trend continuing, citing a force of about 190,000 soldiers.

sections.text: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said the Bundeswehr can likely cover its staffing needs without restoring conscription, Deutschlandfunk and BR24 reported, citing his remarks to Funke Medien [1][2]. He said the force now has about 190,000 soldiers, its highest level in 13 years [2]. If that course continues, there will be no force-growth problem and no need to debate a draft of any design, he said [1][2]. He said he understands young people who protest conscription and worry about war [1]. Strong forces are needed to deter fighting so Germany never has to fight, he said [1][2].
Confidence is high: the defense minister is on the record via Funke, carried by DLF and BR24.

items.title: Germany's CDU and CSU Are Set to Back Ilse Aigner for President
items.lede: ARD reports a planned Monday nomination of Ilse Aigner, with SPD leader Lars Klingbeil signaling conditional support.

sections.text: ZDF and Stuttgarter Zeitung reported on 6 November that Bavarian parliament speaker Ilse Aigner is set to become the Union's presidential candidate [3][4]. They cited CDU sources and reports by Der Spiegel and Süddeutsche Zeitung [3][4]. If elected, Aigner would succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier [3][4]. ARD's capital studio later reported that CDU and CSU plan to propose Aigner, with a formal unveiling expected Monday [5]. CDU presidency and board are to decide Monday; Merz hosts a presidency dinner Sunday evening [5]. SPD leader Lars Klingbeil said the SPD would welcome and support a Union choice of Aigner [5]. Greens' Britta Haßelmann signaled openness to a first woman president while calling Merz's search undignified [5]. DW and POLITICO Europe carried the same Union track [6][7]. POLITICO says it and its source, BILD, belong to the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network [7]. The nomination is not yet an official party resolution [5].
Confidence is high that multiple outlets, including ARD, report an internal Union decision; confidence is moderate that Monday's formal announcement will match, until parties speak on the record.

items.title: German Police Seek Person Linked to Leipzig Airport Drone Case
items.lede: The Federal Criminal Police published an AI image of a hooded e-bike rider near the August explosive-drone find beside Ukrainian cargo planes.

sections.text: Germany’s Federal Criminal Police and federal prosecutor sought tips about a person linked to the early-August Leipzig/Halle explosive-drone incident [8][9][10]. FAZ/dpa, RTL, and Stuttgarter Zeitung reported the appeal [8][9][10]. The BKA said it has identified two suspects and that a third unknown person may also be tied to the attack [8][9]. An AI-generated image shows a slim e-bike rider near Rabutz–Beuditz and Schkeuditz between 31 July and 4 August [8][9]. The person wore dark pants, a thick jacket, black gloves, a large black backpack, a hood, and a low cap: unusually warm summer clothes [8][9]. Investigators say they found a likely launch site near Rabutz–Beuditz and further suspected tools near Radefeld/Lützschena [8]. Airport staff found the drone on the south runway near Ukrainian Antonov freighters on the night of 4–5 August; RTL reported that the explosive apparently failed to detonate because its detonator had torn off [9]. Berlin officially blames Russia; RTL, citing Spiegel, reported that security circles attribute the plot to Russia's GRU [9].
Confidence is high on the manhunt facts from the BKA; the GRU attribution remains an assessment reported by outlets, not a courtroom finding.

items.title: Germany's Merz Speaks With Trump on Ukraine
items.lede: Berlin says any peace deal needs NATO consensus and that talks on Europe's security require European participation.

sections.text: Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Friedrich Merz spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump overnight into 6 November about Russia’s war on Ukraine [11][12]. N-tv reported this; Ukrainska Pravda relayed it [11][12]. Kornelius said Berlin and Washington agree the war must end first and nothing is agreed until everything is [11]. NATO partners must agree, and Europe must participate because its core security is involved, he said [11]. He said negotiations on Europe's security and Ukrainian peace without European participation would not be effective from Berlin's view [11]. Trump floated a "very large" deal after saying he met Kirill Dmitriev [11]. Kornelius said Berlin is informed and Merz is involved in Trump’s thinking [11]. Abu Dhabi talks involving Ukraine are due next week [11][12].
Confidence is high: the call and four points come from the federal government spokesman on the record.

items.title: Germany Opens Trial of Banned 'Kingdom of Germany' Leaders in Düsseldorf
items.lede: Self-styled "king" Peter Fitzek and three co-defendants face criminal-organization and tax charges as the higher regional court begins 52 hearing days.

sections.text: The trial of four alleged "Kingdom of Germany" leaders opened in Düsseldorf on 6 November, WDR and Deutschlandfunk reported [13][14]. Defendants include Peter Fitzek, 61, who styled himself the group's sovereign; he told the court he is "Peter the First" and a citizen of the "Kingdom," and denied tax evasion [15]. Federal prosecutors accuse the four of leading a criminal organization, and tax offenses; the indictment alleges about 10 million euros in undeclared intake and more than 2 million euros in unpaid taxes between 2020 and 2025 [15]. The group ran shadow banks, insurers, and registration offices with fantasy IDs in Dresden, Ulm, Menden, and Wittenberg, prosecutors say [15]. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt banned the Reichsbürger and self-administrator network in May 2025; authorities then estimated about 1,000 adherents versus the group's claim of about 6,000 [15]. Defense lawyers said the case should be ordinary economic crime, not a state-security case, and should be heard by a different court [15]. Fitzek's lawyers say he denies wrongdoing; 52 hearing days are scheduled through September 2027 [15][14].
Confidence is high on the opening and charges from ARD/WDR and DLF courtroom reporting. No verified clock for the opening hour is used here; allegations remain unproven.

items.title: Bosch Sells Part of Its Schwäbisch Gmünd Plant While Keeping a Lease
items.lede: Germany's Bosch is selling Werkteil 2 in the Schießtal as it cuts jobs and restructures the Baden-Württemberg site.

sections.text: German auto supplier Bosch is selling Werkteil 2 at its Schwäbisch Gmünd site in Baden-Württemberg and will remain a partial tenant, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported on 6 November [16]. The site is being restructured as the company cuts many jobs there [16]. Full buyer identity and price sat behind StZ's meter this run; commercial details remain incomplete until a second outlet or company release [16].
Confidence is moderate: the sale headline is on StZ with a named byline, but the paywall blocked full commercial terms this run.
